ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 2 — Focused Visit (Follow-up) — Wilma Rudolph — True-date frame: synthetic events are moved into the patient's historical lifetime. Codes, instruments, and treatments remain modern and are anachronistic.

code.originalText: MRI result: left frontal mass with edema; dexamethasone, CT staging, neuro-oncology consultation with neurosurgery, and preparation for awake craniotomy

text.paragraph: Ms. Rudolph returns three days after her first visit. The MRI the next morning showed a 3.8 cm ring-enhancing mass in the left posterior frontal lobe with central necrosis, surrounding edema and 5 mm of midline shift. Dr. Haynes-Whitaker telephoned her the same afternoon and started dexamethasone 4 mg twice a day with famotidine. Since then the morning headaches have eased and her words come more easily, though she still pauses now and then; the right hand is a little steadier. CT of the chest, abdomen and pelvis yesterday showed no cancer elsewhere. She has had no seizure, vomiting or drowsiness. She saw Dr. Brzezinski of neuro-oncology this morning, together with the neurosurgery team. She is not driving. She said that as a child she was told she would never walk, and that she wants the facts as they are. She has had no thoughts of self-harm. [S]

Three weeks of headaches on waking, with ten days of pauses in finding words and clumsiness of the right hand, in a previously well woman of 54: an intracranial lesion must be excluded. MRI of the brain with and without contrast booked for tomorrow morning, and neuro-oncology review booked
S — Synthetic presenting problem; no symptom of her real illness was made public. Superseded when the MRI showed a brain mass.

Left posterior frontal ring-enhancing mass, 3.8 cm, with central necrosis, surrounding edema and 5 mm midline shift, next to the language and motor areas; presumed high-grade glioma, with no primary cancer elsewhere on CT; tissue diagnosis pending

Neoplasm of unspecified behavior of brain

list.item:
Left posterior frontal ring-enhancing mass, presumed high-grade glioma (D49.6). A single ring-enhancing mass with necrosis and raised perfusion in a woman of 54 with no cancer elsewhere on CT is most likely a high-grade glioma; a solitary metastasis, lymphoma or abscess is much less likely on the imaging. Tissue is needed for the diagnosis, and removing as much tumor as is safe improves outcome. Dr. Brzezinski and the neurosurgery team recommend an awake craniotomy with language and motor mapping in six days, after functional MRI with tractography. Fit for surgery: blood count, chemistry and clotting normal. [S]
Functional MRI with tractography in four days.
Awake craniotomy with mapping in six days; the operating team will explain the awake part in advance.
Tissue for the integrated WHO CNS5 diagnosis, including IDH, TERT, EGFR, chromosome 7 and 10 and MGMT promoter methylation.

Vasogenic cerebral edema with 5 mm midline shift (G93.6). The edema, not the tumor alone, explains much of the headache and the speech and hand symptoms, and both are better on dexamethasone. Glucose 138 mg/dL (not fasting) and white cells 11.8 are the expected effects of the steroid. No antiseizure drug is needed because she has had no seizure. [S]
Continue dexamethasone 4 mg twice a day with famotidine until surgery, then taper.
Seizure first aid explained; call 911 for a seizure lasting more than five minutes.

New headache, word-finding pauses and right-hand clumsiness (R29.818). Explained by the mass and edema found on MRI; superseded. [S]
Problem resolved.

Follow-up: Functional MRI in four days and surgery in six. Primary care review about three weeks after surgery with the pathology. Go to the emergency department for a seizure, worsening speech or weakness, vomiting or drowsiness. Next scheduled visit 1994-07-29: review three weeks after awake craniotomy: pathology and molecular diagnosis, steroid taper, steroid-related hyperglycemia, falls, and the plan for radiotherapy with temozolomide. [S]
